column1: # maddi rename name-map — org.e2immu -> io.codelaser.maddi, target release 0.9.1
# FORMAT   from <TAB> to [<TAB> scope-glob]
#          Lines starting with '#' are comments. '## SECTION <id>' opens a section.
#          A scope-glob (fnmatch against the repo-relative path) limits a rule to
#          matching files; absent means "every text file not frozen by section 4".
# MATCHING rename.py compiles sections 1+1b+3 into ONE alternation sorted by
#          descending source length, so `org.e2immu.analyzer-plugin` wins over
#          `org.e2immu.analyzer` and `org.e2immu.testwrite` over `org.e2immu.test`.
#          Every match requires a trailing (?![A-Za-z0-9_]), so an unmapped token
#          like `org.e2immu.wibble` is left alone and caught by `verify` rather
#          than being silently half-renamed.
# Measured 2026-08-05: 163 source packages, 1,669 java files, zero target collisions.

# content means 100%-similarity renames, which merge cleanly. Combining the move
# and the substitution into one commit defeats git rename detection across 1,669
# files and is what turns a replay into a conflict.

# DECIDED: go ahead (2026-08-05). Rehearsed; ~90% done, 8 tests outstanding — see
# RUNBOOK "Rehearsal 3". The objection below was raised and OVERRULED: the
# published-artifact exposure is theoretical, no consumer is known. Recorded
# because the dependency-free invariant is still checked before every release and
# the split changes that check — not to re-litigate the decision.
# The split was proposed to spare users a support runtime they do not need when
# they only want @Docstring. PUBLISHING.md and maddi-support/build.gradle.kts say
# there is no such runtime to spare them:
#   * `io.codelaser:maddi-support` is ALREADY on Maven Central (0.9.0, 2026-07-22,
#     Apache-2.0; 0.8.2, 2025-08-18, LGPL-3.0) and IS the user-facing annotations
#     artifact. Users compile against exactly this coordinate today.
#   * It is deliberately DEPENDENCY-FREE: it does not apply java-library-conventions,
#     its module-info has NO `requires`, and the release checklist is "the POM must
#     have no <dependencies> and all four module-metadata variants must be empty".
#     That rule was learned the hard way publishing 0.9.0 — the internal
#     io.codelaser:platform BOM is not on Central, so a POM carrying it is
#     unresolvable for a consumer.
#   * It is the only module targeting Java 17 (the rest is 25/26), precisely
#     because it is the one library a user's own code compiles against.
# Splitting would give maddi-support a `requires` on maddi-annotation, i.e. a
# <dependencies> entry in the published POM — breaking the invariant that is
# checked before every release — and would move the annotations out of the
# coordinate that consumers already depend on. The support classes are small and
# import nothing outside java.base, so there is no weight to shed.
# Resolution: `maddi-support` gains exactly ONE dependency, on `maddi-annotation`,
# published to Central alongside it. That POM still resolves — the invariant's real
# purpose was to keep the UNRESOLVABLE internal `platform` BOM out. Update
# PUBLISHING.md's "no <dependencies>" check to "no dependency outside the release
# train" before the next release, or it will fail on a correct artifact.
# Coupling verified one-way: annotation imports only java.lang.annotation and
# itself (zero deps); support imports annotation; nothing imports back.
# SHAPE AS BUILT:
#   maddi-annotation  module io.codelaser.maddi.annotation  (no `requires` at all)
#     exports annotation{,.eventual,.type,.method,.rare}, Java 17, zero deps
#   maddi-support     module io.codelaser.maddi.support
#     exports support, annotatedapi
#     requires transitive io.codelaser.maddi.annotation
#     api(project(":maddi-annotation")) in build.gradle.kts
# ⛔ THE `requires transitive` IS LOAD-BEARING. Because of it, all 21 existing
#    `requires io.codelaser.maddi.support` clauses keep resolving the annotations,
#    so NO consumer module-info needs to change. Drop the `transitive` and the
#    triage table below becomes 21 mandatory edits instead of zero.
#   io.codelaser:maddi-annotation  module io.codelaser.maddi.annotation
#     exports annotation{,.eventual,.type,.method,.rare}
#   io.codelaser:maddi-support     module io.codelaser.maddi.support
#     exports support, annotatedapi
#     requires transitive io.codelaser.maddi.annotation
# 22 maddi module-info.java files `requires org.e2immu.util.external.support`.
# ⛔ DO NOT USE THIS TABLE TO DROP A `requires`. It is a TEXTUAL scan, and a module
#    can use a type it never NAMES — maddi-cst-io reads `io.codelaser.maddi.support`
#    as "NEITHER" here, yet calls .getRight() on an `Either` handed to it by another
#    module's API, so dropping its requires broke the build. Tried and reverted,
#    rehearsal 3. Only the compiler knows; the table is for deciding what a module
#    NEEDS, never for proving what it can lose.
# `rename.py split-triage` re-derives this from the working tree and separates main
# from test usage — only main-source usage belongs in the module descriptor; test
# usage is a testImplementation concern.
# Verified against the tool, 2026-08-05:
#   BOTH:            aapi-archive cst-api cst-impl inspection-api
#                    inspection-parser inspection-resource modification-analyzer
#                    modification-prepwork support util
#   ANNOTATION ONLY: cst-print ide-daemon java-bytecode modification-common
#   SUPPORT ONLY:    inspection-integration java-parser
#   NEITHER, drop the requires: cst-analysis cst-io graph
#   NEITHER in main, but TEST still needs the dependency — drop from
#   module-info AND add a testImplementation entry, or the test compile breaks:
#                    aapi-parser java-openjdk modification-link
# Plus ~9 more `requires` across the six private repos.
